Locate the Power button on the router.
Press the button to power off the device.
Wait for 10–15 seconds.
Press the Power button again to turn it back on.
Method 2: Reboot by disconnecting the power adapter
Unplug the router’s power adapter.
Wait for 10–20 seconds to allow the internal capacitors to discharge.
Plug the power adapter back in.

column2: [LSP Laptop] - LSP Laptop can not display to screen
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue Description: The user reported that the laptop failed to detect or output a signal to an external monitor despite a secure physical connection.
Root Cause: Outdated and pending system drivers. Specifically, critical Intel Graphics Extensions, Realtek Media components, and OEM Firmware (Dell) were stuck in a "Pending Install" state, causing a communication breakdown between the Windows Display Manager and the hardware output ports.


Tên Driver / Thành phần
Vai trò đối với lỗi màn hình
Intel Corporation - Extension - 32.0.101.6881
Cung cấp các tính năng bổ trợ cho Graphics Driver để điều khiển màn hình phụ.
Dell Inc. - Firmware - 0.1.25.1
Cập nhật BIOS/UEFI để sửa lỗi nhận diện cổng HDMI/DisplayPort/Thunderbolt.
Intel - SoftwareComponent - 2512.7.1.0
Thành phần phần mềm điều hướng luồng dữ liệu đồ họa giữa OS và phần cứng.
Intel - System - 2.2.10205.3620
Quản lý tài nguyên hệ thống, đảm bảo cổng kết nối được cấp đủ điện và băng thông.
Realtek - Media / AudioProcessing
(Ảnh hưởng gián tiếp) Điều khiển âm thanh đi kèm qua cổng HDMI/DisplayPort của màn hình.
Resolution Steps:
Accessed Settings > Windows Update.
Identified a backlog of hardware-specific updates (Intel Extension 32.x, Dell Firmware 0.1.25.1).
Executed a full "Install All" operation to clear the update queue.
Performed a system restart to initialize the new firmware and driver stacks.
Outcome: Video signal was successfully restored to the external monitor immediately following the update application and reboot.

column2: [Outlook] - Issue with rule to forward email
column12: P3  (This represent an issue impact to area or group and have working around)
column31:
Issue Resolution Report – Mail Loss on Microsoft 365 Group
End‑user mailbox: user@lsp.com
 Target Group: lsp_ordermanagement_freight@lsp.com
 (Microsoft 365 Group / Distribution)
User‑created Outlook Rule
Rule condition: If sent to this group → forward to manata_mail@scg.com
Rule active time: 03:54, 10/… → 09:35, 11/… (GMT+7)
Symptoms
During the time the rule was active, the Microsoft 365 Group and all group members did not receive external emails.
Message Trace / NDR Findings
Error returned:
550 5.7.193 UnifiedGroupAgent; Delivery failed because the sender isn't a group member
or external senders aren't permitted to send to this group.

Root Cause Analysis
The timeframe when emails were “lost” matches exactly the period when the user rule was active.
Message Trace for that period consistently shows error 5.7.193, which is the expected blocking behavior of UnifiedGroupAgent when an Outlook rule interferes with Group delivery policy.
After disabling the rule → No more 5.7.193 errors → external mail flows normally to the Group.
Recovery of Missing Emails
With error 5.7.193, emails are rejected at transport level.
Rejected messages do not enter the mailbox’s Recoverable Items folder → therefore cannot be restored from the tenant side.
Only possible recovery method:
 Use Message Trace to identify senders → Contact them and request resend.
